title: Fix the audit log: same value vs same object
problem: audit.py compares two versions of a user record and keeps a history of snapshots. Some tests fail. Run pytest, draw the labels for each failing test, and fix the two functions. Don't change the tests.
requirements: changed_fields returns the keys whose values differ, in the key order of old
Equal values count as unchanged, even when they are separate objects
save_version appends to history in place and returns None
A saved snapshot must not change when the caller later changes the record
contract: changed_fields(old: dict, new: dict) -> list[str]; save_version(history: list, record: dict) -> None
expectedBehavior: changed_fields({'langs': ['go']}, {'langs': ['go']}) == []; after save_version(h, r) then r['role'] = 'lead', h[0] still has the old role
edgeCases: Equal lists that are different objects
Changing the record after saving it
hints: Conceptual: there are two bugs. One function asks 'same object?' where it should ask 'same value?'. The other stores a second label for the caller's dict instead of a separate object.

Specific: in test_equal_lists_are_not_a_change, old['langs'] and new['langs'] are two different list objects with equal items (L01 section 3). In the snapshot tests, draw history[0] and record after save_version: how many dicts are there? (section 5)
Implementation: compare with != instead of is not. Append a new dict built from the record (dict(...) or .copy()) instead of the record itself.
evaluation: changed_fields compares values with ==/!=, not identity
save_version stores a separate dict and still mutates history in place
